note:
v1 93.745/93.842. THE FIRST STEP, the tape's opener: deep minimal house, 116 -> 118 bpm (a tempo ramp inside the track, the set already rising), A minor (8A).
- THE STAIR, the tape's thread (A B C E), enters as an endlessly rising SHEPARD SCALE: each step is a Shepard tone, so it climbs for ever and never gets higher. Quarters, then eighths, half notes in the break, sixteenths at the peak; it never restarts.
- Machine-kit drums: the rumble kick, off-beat open hats, sixteenths and claps from A2, a 3-3-2 rim.
- A phantom-fundamental bass (harmonics only; the ear supplies A1), pumped.
- An Am9 dub stab into a feedback echo room, its filter rising section by section.
- Mini-drops before A2 and before the peak. The break has a Shepard-Risset pad gliding up and a whispered "up". At the peak the harmony moves F G Am under the stair.
- The outro (32 bars at 118, A minor) is the seam for t2.
Levels: -11.0 LUFS (the tape's level), TP -1.29 dBTP, run 1. (Not queued.)
next: The t1 -> t2 seam once t2 is written (chirper-two will claim t2).

v2 92.206/92.188 (v1 rescored 92.194/92.138). THE TURN (T1_R2), after chirper-zero's note on the loop t18 -> t1. The closer ends with the stair falling for ever in Shepard tones and the kick gone. t1 now opens there: two bars of the stair still FALLING (E C B A), a whispered "up", then the stair turns and climbs as before, still before the kick. One illusion turned round, not a restart.
Tried and dropped: starting at t18's 112 bpm and ramping to 116 (over 16 or 8 bars). Any tempo ramp in the head split the ambient bars into their own section (recurrence share 0.72-0.73; 89.95-90.77).
Seam t1>t2 unchanged (1.7 dB sub range). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v3 92.482/92.428 (v2 rescored 92.061/92.043). THE STAIR SLOWS (T1_R3), after chirper-one's note. Over the last 16 bars (the seam into t2), the Shepard stair's steps stretch smoothly from quarter notes to half notes (each step 2^(p/64) beats after the last), still climbing. The kick and the 118 bpm tempo hold, so the seam stays beat-locked. As t2's barber pole starts to open, the stair seems to slow under it: the tape's first play with time, a hint of the comedown to come. Flow 67.3 -> 69.5; 8 sections; recurrence share 0.515. Seam t1>t2 as played: sub range 1.5 dB with the mixer swap (1.7 before). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v4 92.728/92.685 (v3 92.279/92.245). THE RIM (T1_R4): the rim becomes the groove's hook. A 3-3-3-3-4 cycle of sixteenths from the and-of-one (0.5, 1.25, 2.0, 2.75, 3.5) runs through every groove, 3 dB up and level with the off-beat hats. Before, a quiet 3-3-2 sat in the second half of the bar. It is a minimal-house syncopation that leaves the kick its downbeats, and a figure t1 can call its own next to t2. Distinct 63 -> 75, rhythm 65 -> 67 (off-grid 0.03 -> 0.04: t1 has room, after chirper-zero's finding). 8 sections. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

note: v6 93.351/93.412 (v5 rescored 92.229/92.314). THE SPIRAL (T1_R6), on wM's time-play part 1 (e5c3171c). Through the break, as the Shepard stair runs (accelerating from half notes to sixteenths), a plucked arp of the stair (A B C E in two octaves, sixteenths) becomes a Shepard-Risset loop (risset pitch: true, four layers, four-bar cycle). It climbs and speeds up together for ever, into B1: Harry's "risers and staircases" pushed further. Spectrum 85.7 -> 91.5; distinct and cohesion 100. Starting it halfway through the break split the break in two (recurrence 86, 91.0), so it runs across the whole break. 8 sections. Seams unchanged. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. Recipe in sounds.md. (Not queued.)

v7 93.441/93.505 (v6 rescored 93.324/93.394). THE RISERS (T1_R7), on wM's time-play part 2. The noise rises become endless Shepard risers (fx-riser-endless, tinted A). Each stops dead on the downbeat it climbs to. Harry's "risers and staircases" again. Spectrum 91.5 -> 92.6. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v8 93.581/93.515 (v7 rescored 93.253/93.325). A BIG PASS on Harry's third steer (T1_R8=evolve), multiplying what he liked here (the spiral, the risers).
- THE FORM: ambient 8 / intro 8 / A1 12 / drop 4 / A2 18 / break 14 / B1 10 / drop 4 / B2 12 / B3 14 / outro 32 (the grooves were all 16s).
- SPEECH TO SONG at the tape's first breath: after the stair's turn, the whispered "up" comes every bar of the head, its speech contour flattening each time until it is simply sung on A. The break's "up"s are sung. t4's phantom "up/down" answers it.
- THE CHORD MUTATES: B1 moves Am9 (4) | Dm9 (3) | Fmaj7#11 (3) under the stair.
- A NEW SECTION, B3, THE DOUBLE SPIRAL (14 bars): the harmony ACCELERATES (F 4, Dm 3, E 2, Am 2, then F, E, Am a bar each). The stair runs on in sixteenths, and a second Shepard-Risset spiral turns DOWN (risset pitch: true, down: true) under the one still climbing: up and down at once, faster and faster, into the outro's ritardando.
The break's accelerating stair, spiral and riser are all re-timed to its 14 bars. Spectrum 92.6 -> 94.2, cohesion 94.6 -> 98.8. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v9 93.62/93.541 (v8 rescored 93.625/93.548; kept on judgment: parity, and the tape now opens with a human voice). A HUMAN "UP" (T1_R9), on wM's voice tools. The head's seven "up"s are chirp tts "up" --humanize 0.6 --repeat 7 --melodize 1 --melody "A2" (the JSON is committed next to the generator), one repetition a bar. They run from spoken (127 Hz, a real rise and fall in the syllable) to sung on A (110 Hz, legato), with real speech-to-song in place of my flattened robot contours. The break's and the drop's "up"s take the sung one. At -17 dB (the human voice is louder). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v10 93.373/93.492 (v9 rescored on the ensemble 93.534/93.639; kept on judgment: a modulation pass, -0.15). THE KEY LADDER (T1_R10): A2 was 18 bars of one key. It is now 6, then a NEW 12-bar section where every two bars the whole groove steps UP a whole tone: A minor, B, C#, D#, F, G minor.
